description: Turn a place (address, POI, town) into coordinates. Ask two ways, and they combine: `query` is free text, one run-together string, the way a person types into a search box, and `street`, `housenumber`, `city`, `postcode` and `country` name the parts of an address separately. At least one of the two is required. Pass the parts whenever you already hold the address in parts (a form, a CRM row, a manifest): components are REQUIREMENTS, not hints, so `city: "London"` means a result outside London cannot come back at all, where "London" inside `query` only reorders. `country` takes an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code or a country name ("GB", "United Kingdom"); a value naming no country is refused rather than silently matching nothing. Returns up to `limit` (default 10) candidates with name, one-line label, lat/lon, type and address parts. Pass `focus` {lat, lon} to rank results near a location higher. A bare city or town name (no comma) lists that city's airports and main railway stations directly behind it, ahead of namesakes elsewhere. Each hit also carries `match`: a per-component matched/inferred/unmatched verdict, the `score_gap` to the runner-up, and which backend answered. READ IT before acting on an address, an unmatched or inferred postcode on the top hit means the answer does not carry the address you asked for, and a small `score_gap` means the ranking barely chose, so show the alternatives instead of picking one. Use `verify_places` when the address came from a model or a user and needs checking rather than using. Results are matched in `lang` (default "en"), so English exonyms ("Munich", "Cologne", "Geneva") resolve to the place meant; pass `lang` when querying in another language, or "default" for each place's local name. Pass `include_entrances: true` to also get each place's `id` and its `entrances`: doors mapped in OpenStreetMap and tied to the place on evidence, each with `kind`, `wheelchair`, `confidence` and `basis`. None is estimated today, and an empty list means no door is tied to the place, not that it has none; `entrances_index` says whether this deployment has an entrance index at all, and `entrances_label` says this for relaying. The `id` feeds `place_entrances` and `route`'s `arrive_at`. Entrances need the MapMap gateway.

LatLon.description: A WGS84 coordinate in decimal degrees: a {lat, lon} object (preferred), or a GeoJSON [lon, lat] array with LONGITUDE FIRST, the same order as every polygon field on this server.

city.description:
Structured component: town or city, e.g. "London". Matches the
containing city as well as the immediate locality, so a suburb name
works here too.

country.description:
Structured component: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code or country name,
"GB", "gb", "United Kingdom" and "UK" all mean the same country.
A value naming no country is refused rather than quietly applied as
a filter that matches nothing.

focus.description: Optional location bias: results near this point rank higher.

housenumber.description:
Structured component: house number, e.g. "10" or "221B". Only
meaningful alongside `street`, a house number on its own excludes
nearly everything and identifies nothing.

include_entrances.description:
Also return each place's `id` and its doors (`entrances`) as
mapped in OpenStreetMap and tied to the place on evidence (default
false). None is estimated today, and an empty list means no door
is tied to the place, not that it has none. Needs the MapMap
gateway.

lang.description:
Language of the place names to match and return, as a two-letter
code. Defaults to "en", which is what makes English exonyms
("Munich", "Cologne", "Geneva") resolve to the place meant rather
than a same-named town elsewhere. Set it to the language your
query is written in; "default" asks for each place's own local
name. Deployments support a fixed set (this one: "en", "de",
"fr"), and anything outside it is refused.

limit.description:
Maximum number of results (default 10): 1–10 on the hosted MapMap
server, 1–50 on a self-hosted server that calls Photon directly.

postcode.description:
Structured component: postcode in any spacing or case, "SW1A 2AA"
and "sw1a2aa" are one query. A bare UK outward code ("SW1A")
selects the whole district.

query.description:
Free-text place query, e.g. "Dover ferry terminal". Required unless
at least one structured component is supplied.

street.description:
Structured component: street name, e.g. "Downing Street". Matches
the street of addresses and POIs (transliterated street names
included) as well as the street itself.

name: geocode

entrances.description:
The place's doors as mapped in OpenStreetMap, returned with
`include_entrances: true`. Empty means no door is tied to the
place, not that it has none; absent means the hit has no place id
to look doors up by.

id.description:
The place id (e.g. `osm:w123:poi`), returned with
`include_entrances: true`: pass it to `place_entrances`, or as
`arrive_at.place_id` on `route`.

label.description: Human-readable one-line label assembled from the address parts.

match.description:
How far this hit can be trusted to be the place that was asked
for, see [`GeocodeMatch`]. Present whenever the MapMap gateway
answered; absent on a deployment falling back to the direct Photon
geocoder, and absent on the gateway's own fast paths (a pasted
coordinate pair, a bare UK outward code, a category browse), which
answer without a ranking to report on.

name.description: Place name, when the source feature has one.

type.description:
Feature type, e.g. "house", "street", "city" (falls back to the
OSM value when the endpoint does not classify).

GeocodeMatch.description:
How well one geocoding result answers what was actually asked.

Geocoding's real failure mode is not "no answer" but a confident answer
to a different question: a plausible row on the wrong street, with
nothing in the response to say so. This object is that missing say-so,
and an agent should read it before acting on an address.

How to read it:

* Any component `unmatched` or `inferred` on the TOP hit means the
  answer does not carry the address that was asked for, an `unmatched`
  postcode means the result has no postcode at all, `inferred` means it
  has a different one. Neither is a match. Say so rather than presenting
  the hit as the address, and reach for `verify_places` when the address
  came from a model or a user and needs checking rather than using.
* A small `score_gap` means the ranking barely chose between this hit
  and the runner-up, which is exactly when to show the alternatives
  instead of picking one for the user.

components.description:
Per-component verdict on this hit: one entry for each structured
component supplied, and empty when the query was free text only.

score_gap.description:
The top result's score minus the runner-up's, rounded to 3 decimal
places. `0` for a single result, and `0` from the `photon` source,
which publishes no per-result score, so a `0` is "no signal", not
"a tie".

source.description:
Which backend answered: "mapmap-index" (the first-party index) or
"photon".

GeocodeMatchComponents.description:
Per-component verdicts inside a [`GeocodeMatch`]. Each is one of
"matched", "inferred" or "unmatched"; a component that was not supplied
is absent entirely.

* "matched", the result's own field carries the value asked for (case-
  and accent-insensitive, and by containment, so `city: "London"`
  matches "City of London").
* "inferred", the result carries a value for that component, but not
  the one asked for. It reached the page through ranking, as when a
  street is found by its transliterated name and displayed under its
  canonical one.
* "unmatched", the result carries no value for that component at all.

PlaceEntrance.description:
One door of a place, as the gateway's `include=entrances` and
`GET /v1/places/{id}/entrances` list it.

Every door served today is a node mapped in OpenStreetMap and tied to
the place on evidence (`source: "osm"`); none is estimated. An empty
list of these means no door is tied to the place, never that the place
has no entrance.

basis.description:
What tied the door to the place: `own_outline`, `stop_area`,
`address_match` or `sole_occupant`.

confidence.description:
How sure the tie between this door and the place is: `high`,
`medium` or `low`. It grades the association, not the door.

ref.description: `ref` as mapped (a station exit number, a door letter).

source.description:
`osm` for a door mapped in OpenStreetMap. `estimated` is reserved
for a door MapMap would infer; none is served today.

wheelchair.description:
`wheelchair=*` as mapped (`yes`, `limited`, `no`, ...); absent when
the map does not say, which is not the same as step-free.

entrances_index.description:
With `include_entrances`: whether this deployment has an entrance
index (`loaded`, `not-configured` or `failed`). Anything but
`loaded` means no hit could carry doors, which is not the same as
the places having none.

entrances_label.description:
With `include_entrances`: what the door lists are and are not.
Pass it on with them.

title: Geocode a place
